name: National Insurance Number (NINO)
issuer: the Isle of Man Income Tax Division
note: The Isle of Man's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: everyone of working age (16 to 65) in employment must have a National Insurance number, issued by the Isle of Man Income Tax Division (or HMRC, if the person lived and worked in the UK first); the island's own tax reference number (H and six digits) is a second number not modelled. Read as given on work from 16. The form is the UK's (HMRC's NIM39110, read the same day for GB: two letters, six digits, A to D), a reading flagged: the sheet doesn't print the NINO's form. No fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Isle-of-man: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: The other reference that can be used in the Isle of Man, for individuals, is their National ... All individuals of working age (16-65) in employment are required to have a NINO which is issued ... either by the Isle of Man Income Tax Division or His Majesty’s Revenue & Customs (HMRC)

sources.title: HMRC internal manual, NIM39110 What a NINO looks like
sources.said: A NINO is made up of 2 letters, 6 numbers and a final letter, which is always A, B, C, or D.
